newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Westpac April Australia consumer index off 0.7 pct.
newsitem.headline: Westpac April Australia consumer index off 0.7 pct.

text.p: The Westpac-Melbourne Institute index of consumer sentiment declined slightly in April by 0.7 percent or 0.8 points to 105.4 from 106.2.

This was the first stable outcome from the index after a particularly volatile six month period, and more recently follows a 4.9 percent rise in March after a 7.9 percent drop in February and 6.0 percent jump in January.

"In view of the fact a sharp fall in the index would have been consistent with this recent sequence, a flat result can be interpreted postively, particularly as the survey was run in the wake of figures showing an unexpected contraction in
employment," said Bill Evans, Westpac's General Manager, economics.

The index has settled about 2.0 percent above the average for the last six months of 1996 and is consistent with Westpac's view that consumer spending and retail sales reached their low point of the cycle in the December quarter, the bank said. It expects some moderate recovery in spending through 1997.

"While most of the components of the index have generally improved, there was a decline in confidence regarding economic conditions over the next twelve months, probably attributable to the fall in employment," Evans said.
This measure of confidence is now slightly below the average for the last six months of 1996.

"However, retailers can derive some comfort from the question relating to whether now is a good time to buy major household items. Positive responses are now sharply higher than the average for the last six months of 1996," Evans said.
Westpac's view on official interest rates is that the Reserve Bank will hold the line for the remainder of 1997.

"Financial markets, which are currently expecting rates to be increased near the end of the year will eventually adjust to the likely scenario of no change in official interest rates until at least mid-1998," Evans added.
